topics.title: 任务条件表示与统一学习
topics.question: 不同反馈任务应怎样参与统一表示和信息交互，才能利用互补信号并减少负迁移？
topics.hypothesis: 共享表示、任务 token、路由及学习目标影响跨任务信息流；预测读出可重新设计，通过共享或独立结构及等训练量控制区分收益来源。

topics.title: Compatibility of task conditioning and linear-moment representation
topics.question: Under the frozen inputs and training protocol, can the g3 task-conditioning approach improve four-task macro ROC-AUC over the stronger g0 linear-moment source at justified parameter and measured compute cost?
topics.hypothesis: The source approaches may preserve complementary predictive information, but redundancy or task interference may erase the smaller task-conditioning gain. Inherit the two committed source approaches, subject to implementation inspection in the next phase; test their combination against both frozen source bests, especially g0 at 0.8283262734957326. Cross representation replacement with task-conditioning removal, retain the available gradient-stop contrasts, and compare capacity and equal training exposure while measuring training/inference cost. Added utility predicts a repeat-confirmed macro-AUC improvement over both sources beyond capacity controls. Failure to exceed g0, equivalent gains from capacity alone, or disappearance under replacement controls opposes complementary utility; unchanged stop contrasts would leave gradient isolation unsupported. Report every task AUC/logloss trade-off. Reserve resources for attribution and repeat confirmation; freeze selection and comparison suite before one withheld assessment. No mechanism or novelty is established by the present summaries.

topics.title: Compatibility of memory-joint representation and task conditioning
topics.question: Under the frozen inputs and training protocol, does combining the committed g0 memory-joint representation with the g3 task-conditioning approach exceed both frozen source bests, especially validation four-task macro ROC-AUC 0.8303789178781177, at justified parameter and measured compute cost?
topics.hypothesis: The two committed approaches may preserve complementary information, but their shared representation ancestry may make task conditioning redundant or introduce task interference. Inherit their approaches only after implementation inspection in the next phase. Improvement over both frozen bests and matched-capacity source-replacement/factorial controls, followed by repetition, would support added utility; failure to exceed the stronger source or benefits reproduced by capacity alone would oppose it. Recent unsuccessful mean/copy variants constrain those implementations without refuting task conditioning generally. No novelty or confirmed mechanism is claimed.

topics.title: Transfer of task-private utility to the strongest pair-rank-occupancy representation
topics.question: Under the frozen inputs and training protocol, does the committed task-private approach retain incremental utility on the newer pair-rank-occupancy source, exceeding both frozen source bests, especially validation four-task macro ROC-AUC 0.831886841754755, at justified parameter and measured compute cost?
topics.hypothesis: Nearest available work is the committed pair-rank and task-private summaries plus the unsuccessful exchange/rank contrasts; code and papers are unavailable, and external novelty is unverified. Inherit only the two committed approaches after implementation inspection in the next phase. The proposed difference is testing task-private utility on the newer representation rather than the older memory-joint entry. Task-specific information may remain useful, but shared ancestry, redundancy, task interference, capacity and seed variation are alternative explanations. Preserve both frozen source bests; source-replacement/factorial and matched-capacity controls, with measured training/inference costs, would distinguish compatibility from added capacity if budget permits. Failure to exceed the stronger source weakens this transfer hypothesis; improvement only over the weaker source is insufficient. One positive run supports provisional utility, not a mechanism; controlled attribution and repetition require reserved resources. Freeze selection and comparison suite before a single held-out assessment; withheld outcomes cannot guide further open research.

Both-stop exceeds neither-stop by only 0.000235 AUC, so gradient isolation remains unresolved; these single-seed results are provisional. Prioritize attribution and reserve budget for repeat confirmation and frozen assessment.

topic.title: Transfer of task-private utility to the strongest pair-rank-occupancy representation
topic.question: Under the frozen inputs and training protocol, does the committed task-private approach retain incremental utility on the newer pair-rank-occupancy source, exceeding both frozen source bests, especially validation four-task macro ROC-AUC 0.831886841754755, at justified parameter and measured compute cost?
topic.hypothesis: Nearest available work is the committed pair-rank and task-private summaries plus the unsuccessful exchange/rank contrasts; code and papers are unavailable, and external novelty is unverified. Inherit only the two committed approaches after implementation inspection in the next phase. The proposed difference is testing task-private utility on the newer representation rather than the older memory-joint entry. Task-specific information may remain useful, but shared ancestry, redundancy, task interference, capacity and seed variation are alternative explanations. Preserve both frozen source bests; source-replacement/factorial and matched-capacity controls, with measured training/inference costs, would distinguish compatibility from added capacity if budget permits. Failure to exceed the stronger source weakens this transfer hypothesis; improvement only over the weaker source is insufficient. One positive run supports provisional utility, not a mechanism; controlled attribution and repetition require reserved resources. Freeze selection and comparison suite before a single held-out assessment; withheld outcomes cannot guide further open research.
